subject: Sporadic DB replication stalls over private peering — conntrack & SG suspicion
messages:
From: Alex Harris <alex.harris@brightline.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
Cc: eng-ops@brightline.com
Date: 2026-12-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Intermittent DB replication stalls since private peering cutover

Jasmine / Redwood team,

We cutover the private peering to Redwood's VPC last night (per the cutover plan) and since ~02:30 UTC we've observed periodic stalls in cross-datacenter Postgres replication. Symptoms: replication lag spikes to tens of seconds for ~30-90s, then recovers. Application error rates spike during these windows.

What we've captured so far:
- brief tcp retrans bursts between 10.23.5.12 (primary) -> 10.23.6.34 (replica), SACKs present, lots of retrans.
- some TCP connections show RSTs originating from 198.51.100.17 (Redwood private-edge IP)
- we don't see consistent MTU blackhole signs in traceroutes; PMTU tests are inconclusive

We believe this is happening only on the traffic path that traverses the new peering (other paths between our DCs are fine). Can the Redwood team help triage — suspecting either a security group/fair-queue rate-limit or an ephemeral port / conntrack exhaustion on the peering NAT.

I've attached a light pcap summary and a conntrack snapshot from our side. Happy to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Alex Harris
Sr. Infra Engineer, Brightline Logistics
attachments: pcap-lite-summary.txt, conntrack-dump-20261218.txt
From: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Intermittent DB replication stalls since private peering cutover

Alex — thanks for the quick context and the artifacts. I'm pulling Markus (network infra) and Marissa (Private deploys) in here to triage.

Immediate asks while we dig in:
1) Can you confirm whether your replica connections are pinned to keepalive intervals lower than 30s? Any offload (GSO/GRO) toggles on the DB host?
2) We'll need a conntrack delta matching the spike window if possible (we saw the dump but no timestamp alignment).
3) Can you share the exact /28 on your side that's used for the peering? We want to target flow logs.

Plan: Markus will check edge NAT/conntrack metrics, SG rate-limits, and per-flow packet counters from our peering edge. Marissa will validate the cutover config (SNAT ranges, port-preservation) and whether the traffic is hitting any edge ACLs. We'll reconvene once we have packet counters and conntrack peaks.

If it's helpful we can stand up a short packet mirror for a 1-hour window during a maintenance window to capture full PCAPs.

-Jasmine

From: markus.klein@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-12-19T07:30:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Intermittent DB replication stalls since private peering cutover

Quick update from the edge triage (10:30 - 14:00 UTC capture window):

Findings:
- We correlated flow logs with the windows Alex called out. There are short bursts where the edge device generated TCP RSTs for flows originating from Brightline primary -> replica. RSTs are generated by the edge NAT process when conntrack lookup fails during a transient conntrack table resize event.
- conntrack table on the active edge instance spiked to 94% of configured max during the incident window; source entries were heavily biased to ephemeral ports from Brightline's /28.
- No consistent MTU blackhole: MSS clamping observed on a subset of flows (we have a rule that clamps MSS for BGP-ingress with jumbo suspect), but packet drop patterns align more with conntrack churn than pure fragmentation.
- We don't see SG explicit denies; rather, soft-limits and per-flow rate policing triggered RSTs when a conntrack lookup missed and the flow hit a fast-path rate threshold.

Suggested immediate mitigations (we can implement in a targeted maintenance window):
1) Temporarily increase conntrack_max on the active edge instance by 50% and monitor delta.
2) Disable MSS clamp rule for Brightline prefix to remove extra packet rewrites while we stabilize.
3) Short-term: add a stateful NAT scratch pool to spread new ephemeral allocations across two adjacent edge instances (reduces single-instance pressure).

I'll prepare the exact commands and config diffs. If Brightline can reduce client-side keepalive churn for the next 24h that will help while we adjust capacity.

-Markus
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: edge-flow-log-snippet.txt
From: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
To: Alex Harris <alex.harris@brightline.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, eng-ops@brightline.com
Date: 2026-12-20T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent DB replication stalls since private peering cutover — plan and next steps

Alex — summary and next steps: thanks for the quick handoff and artifacts. We confirmed the primary signal is conntrack pressure on our peering edge with secondary contribution from an MSS clamp rule. We will proceed with the mitigations below in a staged rollout between 17:00-18:00 UTC today (targeted to the peering region only):

Actions we will take (17:00 UTC start):
- Increase conntrack_max on active edge instance from 200k -> 300k (rollback: revert value).
- Deploy a short-lived NAT scratch pool: add 2 ephemeral SNAT prefixes to spread allocations.
- Disable MSS clamp for Brightline prefix during the stabilization window.
- Enable a 1-hour packet mirror to our analysis cluster and share full PCAPs with your team (will redact unrelated traffic).

What we need from Brightline:
- If possible, hold client keepalive interval at >= 60s for the next 12 hours or agree to a maintenance window to lower keepalives temporarily (this reduces ephemeral churn).
- Confirm the peering /28: 10.23.5.0/28 and 10.23.6.32/28? (we'll use these to scope policy changes)

I'll log the JIRA (RED-10234) with the config diffs and post the Drive link with the full PCAP once the mirror finishes. We'll monitor replication lag in your telemetry and keep a 24h watch. If problems persist after the staged changes we'll escalate to a hotfix on the edge firmware and consider scaling more edge capacity.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
